facts.raw_span: A 60‐year‐old tailor with no significant medical history
a 3‐year history of macerated skin between his toes
a painful, fissured ulcer at the base of the fourth interdigital space of the right foot
which had been progressively enlarging over the past 18 months
received multiple antifungal regimens—including topical sertaconazole for 6 weeks and oral terbinafine 250 mg daily for 6 weeks—without improvement
a verrucous, infected ulceration with infiltrated, hyperkeratotic edges and a whitish, fissured base measuring 3 cm in diameter, extending onto the dorsum of the foot
Dermoscopy revealed unstructured whitish areas and hyperkeratosis
Popliteal and inguinal lymph nodes were not palpable
the remainder of the examination was unremarkable

concepts.why: The patient has a 3-year history of macerated skin between his toes and a painful, fissured ulcer at the base of the fourth interdigital space of the right foot, which had been progressively enlarging over the past 18 months.

The patient has a verrucous, infected ulceration with infiltrated, hyperkeratotic edges and a whitish, fissured base measuring 3 cm in diameter, extending onto the dorsum of the foot, and dermoscopy revealed unstructured whitish areas and hyperkeratosis.
The patient received multiple antifungal regimens without improvement, suggesting a possible fungal foot infection.

The patient has a painful, fissured ulcer at the base of the fourth interdigital space of the right foot, which had been progressively enlarging over the past 18 months, and the presence of a verrucous, infected ulceration with infiltrated, hyperkeratotic edges suggests a possible diabetic foot ulcer.

The patient has a verrucous, infected ulceration with infiltrated, hyperkeratotic edges and a whitish, fissured base measuring 3 cm in diameter, extending onto the dorsum of the foot, which could be a sign of squamous cell carcinoma.

rationales.F01: The patient's age and lack of significant medical history do not specifically point to any of the listed conditions.
rationales.F03: The presence of a painful, fissured ulcer at the base of the fourth interdigital space is highly suggestive of Chronic Interdigital Foot Ulcer.
rationales.F05: The lack of improvement with antifungal regimens suggests that Fungal Foot Infection is less likely.
rationales.F06: The description of the ulceration is consistent with both Hyperkeratotic Ulcer and Squamous Cell Carcinoma, but the presence of a verrucous, infected ulceration makes Hyperkeratotic Ulcer more likely.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's 3-year history of macerated skin between his toes and a painful, fissured ulcer at the base of the fourth interdigital space of the right foot, along with the lack of response to antifungal treatments, support the diagnosis of Chronic Interdigital Foot Ulcer. However, the presence of a verrucous, infected ulceration with hyperkeratotic edges and the progressive enlargement of the ulcer over 18 months also raise suspicion for Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
